bug_title: hub: the relay's from-session check only covers prompt, steer and reply, so a relayed sandbox command skips it
defect: The PR added a `sandbox` driver command refused from-session on the session socket, but the hub relay's from-session check (crates/hub/src/relay.rs) is hard-coded to prompt/steer/reply. A session's unconfined shell can therefore relay `sandbox {enabled:false}` through the hub and turn confinement off with no person acting.
how_identified: Issue 4327 names Part 9 (#3635, PR #4308) as the source of the sandbox command whose relay path was left unchecked.

pr_title: tui: first run opens sign-in, then the model picker, on a terminal with nothing set up
bug_title: First run opens sign-in when any provider is logged out, not when all are
defect: The first-run check in crates/tui/src/app/model_picker.rs sets has_credential from `catalogue.logged_out.is_empty()`, which is true only if every installed provider has a credential. A user signed in to one provider but with others installed (e.g. Vertex, which always counts as logged out) gets the /login overlay on every launch, contradicting docs/tui.md.
how_identified: git log -S on `logged_out.is_empty()` in model_picker.rs shows this PR added the line; the issue quotes that exact code.

pr_title: Defer history requests until opening stream passes finish
bug_title: tui: a reopening abandons a history wait without checking whose session it is
defect: The PR introduced `abandon_history(id)`, which marks a history wait abandoned by command id alone, and the reopen path never compares the ended read's session to the reopened one. With two sessions resuming concurrently, reopening one abandons the other's in-flight history answer so its transcript never folds.
how_identified: git log -S 'fn abandon_history' shows this PR added it (later moved by #3739); the same PR's opening-pass gate is also the origin of bug 4444 (pass_open not checked by paging/scroll/recount).

pr_title: Run host.tool as an inner call of the running tool call
bug_title: An inner host.tool result too big for the Lua memory cap fails the outer call instead of returning to the script
defect: In the PR's new `Reply::Tool(Ok(outcome))` arm of resume_values, converting the inner tool result with `to_lua` (lua.create_string) can fail against the extension's memory cap, and that error propagates out of schedule.rs without ever resuming the coroutine. The script cannot pcall it and the whole outer call (e.g. codemode) becomes a ToolError.
how_identified: git log -S 'host.tool' / blame on resume_values' Reply::Tool arm points to this PR; issue 4767 describes the to_lua path it added.

pr_title: Hand off on a context overflow, moving the last step's tool results out
bug_title: Compaction: check the trigger before the first measured reply, and report a failed artifact write
defect: The PR's overflow handling moves tool results into artifacts with `write_artifact(...).ok()?` in compaction/note.rs, so a failed write silently leaves the result inline with no log or notice. The overflow note request can then still not fit and surfaces as an unexplained context_overflow.
how_identified: git log -S '.ok()?' / 'fn artifact_of' in crates/loop shows this PR introduced the silent drop; only the artifact half of 4684 is from this PR (the check_context half is from #710).

pr_title: hub: deleting a session, fiber sessions delete
bug_title: Tell connected terminals when another client deletes or archives a session
defect: The PR's hub delete calls `hub.feed.forget(&id)`, which drops the session from the feed but sends nothing to connected clients. A second terminal keeps showing the deleted session's row and counts until it reconnects, contrary to docs/tui.md's session-list rule.
how_identified: The issue cites Feed::forget and delete.rs:74; git log shows both were added by this PR.
